- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to compensate for downward bias.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model frequently overcorrects downward; cap forecast at 80–82 for 2–3 periods to avoid overshoot.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive drops > 2% from peak), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to reflect earlier trend reversal.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture sentiment-driven momentum; if sentiment shifts sharply, adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to align with sentiment direction.
